newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese inflation seen sinking to record lows.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese inflation seen sinking to record lows.

text.p: Portugal's April CPI data, the lowest in three decades, showed there were no inflationary pressures and suggested that inflation could sink to further record lows in the coming months, analysts said on Wednesday.
Prices rose by 0.2 percent in April against 0.9 percent in April 1996, and the year-on-year rate stood at 1.8 percent, the lowest level since the 1960s, compared with 2.9 percent in April 1996.

The sharp drop had been widely predicted for statistical reasons because in the same month last year, the consumer price index (CPI) was driven higher by rising meat prices provoked by Europe's mad cow disease scare.

"April inflation figures showed that there were no inflationary tensions evident in the economy and that the year-on-year rate will hit bottom next month (May), around 1.5 or 1.6 percent," said Martim Amaral Neto, analyst of Banco ESSI.
Isabel Cabral of Lisbon broker Fincor said: "In May, June and July, the year-on-year rate could drop to 1.4 percent."

Nuno Godinho, analyst of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said: "In December, year-on-year inflation could be slightly higher than two percent, and the average annual rate should close the year at 2.2 percent."
Jose Luiz Alzola, analyst of Salomon Brothers, said: "Without doubt the average annual rate will meet the government's inflation target (2.0-2.5 percent)."
Ten analysts polled by Reuters said the Bank of Portugal had room to cut official rates further and that it could cut rates for the second straight week on Friday.
They said the probability of cutting rates would increase if the Bank of Spain cut its rates.

Last week the Bank of Portugal wrong-footed analysts and trimmed the repo rate by 30 basis points (bp) to 6.0 percent and the draining rate, used to drain excess funds from the money market, by 10 bp to 5.70 percent.
Alzola said he believed that the repo rate could fall to 5.50 percent by the end of the year and the draining rate to 5.20 percent.
